Thought: To determine which species has the smallest concentration in the solution, we need to analyze the dissociation and equilibrium reactions of the compounds involved. NaNO2 is a salt that dissociates completely in water into Na+ and NO2-. Then, NO2- can act as a base and react with water to form HNO2 and OH-. The concentration of Na+ is 0.1 M, as it completely dissociates. The concentration of NO2- initially is also 0.1 M, before any further reactions occur. The reaction of NO2- with water to form HNO2 and OH- is an equilibrium reaction, and the concentration of H3O+ will be affected by the basic nature of NO2-. Since HNO2 is formed from NO2- reacting with water, its concentration will be less than 0.1 M. The concentration of H3O+ will be very low, as the solution is basic. Thus, H3O+ is expected to have the smallest concentration.
